topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer causation, carcinogenicity methodologies, and tumor initiation and promotion.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Basis, Environmental Influences, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and evaluate how intrinsic cellular errors, environmental mutagens, and population-level epidemiological variations determine cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections contribute to cancer development, focusing on the mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma in the context of malaria and Epstein-Barr virus.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental chemicals, dietary toxins, and UV radiation cause DNA damage directly or through host xenobiotic metabolic conversion into reactive mutagens.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Initiation-Promotion Paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics contrast mutagenic initiators with non-mutagenic tumor promoters, demonstrating how chronic inflammation and signaling agonists drive the clonal outgrowth of primed cells.

topics.label: Host Tissue Susceptibility, Developmental Context, and Mechanistic Principles
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cellular proliferative state and developmental stage influence susceptibility to mutagens and summarize the fundamental direct and indirect mechanisms underlying carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal models, and in vitro bacterial assays used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on daily risk-benefit decisions regarding carcinogen exposure and summarizing the primary takeaways.
